minutes.headline: Water district voted to replace the failed pump at Lancaster Avenue well four, paid from the well testing and cleaning accounts.
minutes.summary: The board approved the October 25 minutes, signed warrants, and approved replacing the pump at well number four after cleaning showed it in poor condition. It also discussed lead service line postcards, agreeing to mail the smaller targeted batch first, and agreed to buy two cameras. A newspaper notice about the delayed water main replacement was previewed.

what_happened.line: The board moved to replace the pump at well number four, to be paid from the well cleaning and well testing accounts; the vote count was not audible.
The board agreed to mail the smaller batch of targeted lead service line postcards first, wait about a month, then follow up with non-responders.
The board was agreeable to ordering two security cameras for in-house installation rather than using a higher installer quote.
Warrants were signed, including a first pay request from MDR for their bond only, and one agenda item was taken off the table and rescheduled.
A newspaper notice about the delayed water main replacement will be reviewed and sent to the Ledger.

why_it_matters: Paying for the pump from the well cleaning and testing accounts draws down money set aside for those jobs, and members raised a warrant article at a special or annual meeting to replenish the cleaning account, a vote residents could be asked to take.
The lead service line mailing is how customers are asked to confirm what their service pipe is made of, and members voiced concern that unused state money for this work is lost.
